unified_issues.description: The headline 6x32 step grid cells are plain <div>s with click/contextmenu listeners only — no tabindex, no role (e.g. gridcell/switch), no keyboard handler. The primary interactive surface of the plugin is unreachable and unoperable by keyboard.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Make cells focusable (tabindex) inside a role=grid/row structure, add an aria-label per cell (voice + step + velocity tier), and support Space/Enter to cycle velocity plus Delete to clear; mirror the existing left-click/right-click semantics.

unified_issues.description: Knobs set role='slider' but never set aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuetext, and mute/solo <button>s never set aria-pressed. Screen readers announce a slider/button with no value or toggle state.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: In updateKnobVisual set aria-valuenow (and a human aria-valuetext from the same formatter used for the visible value) on the knob element; in bindToggle reflect st.getValue() into aria-pressed on each button.

unified_issues.description: Multiple labels render below the 12px legibility floor (knob-label 10.5px, knob-value 10px, cell-mark 9px, tr-label/lane-legend/tour-soon 10.5px), which works against the stated projector-readable goal for low-vision viewers.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Raise the smallest functional labels toward 12px (or add a viewport/zoom-friendly rem scale), keeping the dense layout by trimming padding rather than shrinking type below 12px.

unified_issues.description: The plain-language tooltips — the core pedagogy of the teaching UI — are triggered only on pointerenter/pointermove. Keyboard and focus users receive none of the explanatory copy.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Also show/hide the tooltip on focusin/focusout for the same [data-tip] elements and position it relative to the focused element, so keyboard navigation surfaces the same explanations as hover.

unified_issues.description: Preset-tour buttons toggle an 'armed' active style and rewrite the caption on click, presenting themselves as interactive, but are intentionally non-functional Stage-4 hooks. This risks reading as dead/broken controls to a user.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Until Stage 4 wires preset content, visually mark the buttons as not-yet-active (disabled/dimmed affordance or a clear 'preview only' state) so the armed styling does not imply a working action; revisit when presets land.

unified_issues.description: The clearGrid native function is registered in C++ and fetched in JS (clearGridFn) but is never invoked — there is no whole-grid clear affordance in the UI. Harmless, but it is a registered-but-unused bridge binding (inverse of the usual bridge-gap).
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Either expose a 'Clear pattern' control wired to clearGridFn (with a local gridState reset + repaint) or drop the unused fetch to keep the JS<->C++ surface tight.

unified_issues.description: Doc-vs-implementation drift: PLAN T3 and RESEARCH list a getBpm native fn and separate 'playhead'/'triggers' pushed events, but the shipped editor exposes no getBpm native fn and instead pushes a single consolidated 'frame' event (PluginEditor.cpp:204-210) carrying ph/bpm/sync/hits, which app.js consumes via addEventListener('frame'). The implementation is functionally complete and internally consistent (no dead control, no bridge gap); only the planning docs are stale.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Update PLAN.md T3 and RESEARCH.md pushed-events section to describe the single 'frame' event (bpm embedded) and drop the getBpm native fn reference, so the docs match the shipped bridge surface.

unified_issues.description: getVizAnalyzer() returns a non-const OSimpleBeatmaker::VizAnalyzer& to the message-thread editor, exposing the producer-side push()/setPlayheadStepPhase() and bumpFrame() methods that are intended for the audio thread only. The editor uses just the consumer API (drain/getPlayheadStepPhase), so this is not a live defect, but the interface is broader than the message thread should be able to reach.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Either return a const reference and add const consumer-side accessors, or expose a narrow message-thread view (e.g. drainViz()/playheadPhase() forwarders on the processor) so the producer methods are not reachable from the editor.

unified_issues.description: currentSampleRate is a plain (non-atomic) double written in prepareToPlay and read by the editor's 60 Hz Timer (getCurrentSampleRate()), whereas the sibling taps lastKnownBpm/hostSynced are std::atomic. The read/write is a theoretical, benign data race (aligned 64-bit, advisory-only UI scale factor) but is inconsistent with the other two taps.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Promote currentSampleRate to std::atomic<double> with relaxed store/load to match getLastKnownBpm()/isHostSynced() and remove the theoretical race, or document explicitly why a plain double is acceptable for this advisory tap.

unified_issues.description: Stale Stage-1 header comment block states 'No binary-data target this stage (avoids the O-simpleGrain dual-namespace collision until a 2nd target genuinely exists in Stage 3)' and 'No DSP yet', which now contradicts the juce_add_binary_data target added at lines 55-62 and the Stage-2 DSP spine. Documentation-only; does not affect the build.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Update the top-of-file comment to reflect Stage 3 state: a single binary-data target now exists (default BinaryData namespace is correct because it is the only such target), and the DSP spine landed in Stage 2.
